descriptionChirho: Piel stem core cultic sense: to perform a ritual act of atonement or expiation, typically by offering a sacrifice to cover sin and restore the offerer's standing before God — the dominant sense of the root in Levitical legislation; Arabic يُكَفِّرُ (yukaffiru, 'he atones'), Korean 속죄하다 (sokjoe-hada, 'make atonement'), Swahili kufanya upatanisho ('make reconciliation/atonement'), Hindi प्रायश्चित करना (praayashchit karnaa, 'make atonement'), Spanish expiar ('atone/expiate').

Piel stem extended sense: to appease or pacify someone's anger by means of a gift or gesture, used of human-to-human relations rather than cultic ritual — the subject seeks to mollify wrath; Arabic أُكَفِّرُ (ukaffiru, contextually 'I placate'), Korean 달래다 (dallaeda, 'soothe/appease'), Swahili -tuliza ('calm/soothe'), Hindi शान्त करना (shaant karnaa, 'pacify'), Spanish apaciguar ('appease').

Piel stem etymological sense: to cover over or conceal sin or transgression, preserving the root meaning of physical covering — distinct from the developed cultic sense in that the focus is on hiding or blotting out the offense itself; Arabic cognate كَفَرَ (kafara, 'cover/conceal'), Korean 덮다 (deopda, 'cover'), Swahili -funika ('cover'), Hindi ढकना (dhaknaa, 'cover'), Spanish perdonar/cubrir ('forgive/cover').

Piel stem theological sense: to forgive or pardon sin directly as an act of divine or authoritative mercy, without explicit reference to sacrificial ritual — the agent (usually God) grants absolution; Arabic يُكَفِّرُ (yukaffiru, contextually 'forgives'), Korean 용서하다 (yongseo-hada, 'forgive'), Swahili -samehe ('forgive/pardon'), Hindi क्षमा करना (kshamaa karnaa, 'forgive'), Spanish perdonar ('pardon/forgive').

Piel stem extended sense: to avert, ward off, or prevent calamity or punishment — the covering metaphor extended to deflecting harmful consequences rather than covering sin per se; Arabic تَكْفِيرَهَا (takfiiraha, 'its expiation/averting'), Korean 막다 (makda, 'block/prevent'), Swahili -zuia ('prevent/avert'), Hindi टालना (taalnaa, 'avert/ward off'), Spanish expiar/desviar ('expiate/avert').

Passive and reflexive-passive stems: to be atoned for, to have atonement made on one's behalf, or to be forgiven — the passive counterpart of the Piel cultic sense, indicating that sin has been covered or expiated by another's action; Arabic يُكَفَّرُ (yukaffaru, 'it is atoned'), Korean 속죄되다 (sokjoe-doeda, 'be atoned') or 용서되다 (yongseo-doeda, 'be forgiven'), Swahili -fanyiwa upatanisho ('have atonement made for'), Hindi प्रायश्चित होना (praayashchit honaa, 'be atoned'), Spanish ser expiado/perdonado ('be atoned/forgiven').

Pual stem distinct sense: to be annulled, cancelled, or made void — a specialized use where the 'covering' metaphor extends to wiping away or nullifying a covenant or agreement, semantically distant from atonement; Arabic يُبْطَلُ (yubtalu, 'be annulled'), Korean 폐하다 (pyeha-da, 'annul/abolish'), Swahili -vunjwa ('be broken'), Hindi टूटना (tootnaa, 'be broken'), Spanish ser anulado ('be annulled').
